newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar company to seek funds in November.
newsitem.headline: Qatar company to seek funds in November.

text.p: One of Qatar's three major upcoming petrochemical projects will enter the international financial market in November to raise $350 million to fund its construction, a Qatari official said on Wednesday.

"Sometime in November we will be issuing the mandate for raising funds through a loan or bond to finance the construction of Qatar Vinyl Company," the official at the state Qatar General Petroleum Corporation (QGPC) said.

France's Societe Generale has been appointed financial advisor on the full $500 million project which is 25.5 percent owned by QGPC and 31.9 percent owned by its subsidiary Qatar Petrochemical Company.
Other partners are Norsk Hydro of Norway which holds 29.7 percent and Elf Atochem of France, which holds 12.9 percent in the project. Elf Atochem is the chemicals unit of Elf Aquitaine.
The project is designed to produce 338,000 tonnes of ethylene dichloride, 200,000 tonnes of vinyl chloride monomer and 260,000 tonnes of caustic soda annually from 2000.
The company is expected to issue tenders for an engineering, procurement and construction contract in September.

The project is to be funded 70 percent by loans or bonds and 30 percent by equity. Qatar's success in raising $1.2 billion to fund the construction of its Ras Laffan liquefied natural gas company last December has encouraged the oil and gas-rich state to consider issuing global bonds as a option.

Qatar Vinyl Company is the second of the state's three petrochemical joint ventures signed this year with foreign companies to tap its gas reserves -- the third largest in the world after Russia's and Iran's.

One of them -- Qatar Fuel Additive Company (Qafac) -- is already under construction, mainly financed by export credits. The third project -- a $750 million ethylene cracker -- was set up by QGPC as a 51-49 percent joint venture with Phillips Petroleum Co of the United States on May 18.
Qatar Petrochemical Co has been producing ethylene and polyethylene since 1982.
